title: Sprint 3 Reflection and Mid-Course Problem Frame Revision
description: Use AI follow-up questions to make your stakeholder evidence and your Problem Frame revision specific.

questions.prompt: Draft your Sprint 3 reflection. Explain what a real person helped you see that AI did not, what part of your frame changed and why, what tension or conflict you are carrying forward, and what you will validate next.
questions.placeholder: Use your stakeholder map, your Stakeholder Validation Report, and your revised Problem Frame. Separate what a stakeholder actually said from what you inferred from it.
questions.aiContext: This is the Sprint 3 mid-course reflection for Reframing Problems with AI. The participant mapped stakeholders, tested and widened the map in their own AI chat, then held a real validation conversation and revised their Problem Frame. Ask follow-up questions that separate what the stakeholder actually said from the participant's interpretation of it, that catch a frame change with no evidence behind it, and that catch a conflict smoothed into agreement. If two accounts disagree, push them to say what each account is describing rather than averaging the two. A frame the conversation confirmed is a legitimate result, so do not push for a change that the evidence does not support; push instead for what that confirmation rests on. Make what they will validate next specific enough to act on. Do not rewrite the reflection for them.
questions.discussionPrompt: Use these questions to revise so that the stakeholder evidence and the Problem Frame change are both clear.
questions.summaryPlaceholder: Write the final version you want to submit, answering all four questions.
